A 60-year-old female presented to the
neurology services with paraspinal muscle
rigidity, muscle spasms and new onset
scoliosis. Previous history included symp-
tomatic Hashimoto /C213s thyroiditis.
Although initial thyroid stimulating hor-
mone was elevated and free thyroxine
reduced, these remained stable with
thyroxine replacement.
At 62 years, she developed an ataxic
gait with dysmetria and deteriorating
mobility. Overtime oscillopsia developed
impaired reading and writing. By
65 years she was wheelchair bound. Type
1 diabetes mellitus was diagnosed fol-
lowing presentation with diabetic
ketoacidosis. Other complaints included
lower limb myoclonic jerks and
post-prandial abdominal cramps with
dyspepsia.
Neurological examination at presenta-
tion revealed paraspinal rigidity and
scoliosis with exaggerated lumbar
lordosis. Muscle power was normal with-
out fatigue. Reﬂexes were pathologically
brisk with extensor plantar responses.
Subsequent examinations revealed scan-
ning dysarthria, dysmetria and intention
tremor. Opsoclonus was prominent at rest
and in all directions of gaze.
Antiglutamic acid decarboxylase
(GAD) antibody was positive with a titre
of 87 U/ml (range 0–1 U/ml). Antinuclear
antibody was positive with a speckled
pattern (titre: 1/640). Antipancreatic islet
cell, anti-adrenal cortex, antitissue
transglutaminase and anti-endomysial
antibodies were positive. Antithyroid
peroxidase antibody was positive (titre:
>1000 U/ml). Duodenal biopsy demon-
strated villous atrophy. Cortisol levels,
pre- and post-synacthen were normal on
repeated sampling. Adrenocorticotrophic
hormone levels were normal.
Cerebrospinal ﬂuid (CSF) analysis
demonstrated an elevated protein of
0.77 g/l (range 0.15–0.45 g/l), white cells
of 6/cmm (range 0–5/cmm) and normal
glucose. CSF oligoclonal bands were
absent. MRI of brain and spine and CT of
thorax, abdomen and pelvis were normal.
Muscle rigidity/spasms were well
controlled with benzodiazepines. Coeliac
disease was treated by a gluten free diet.
Speciﬁc immune treatment including
oral steroids, intravenous (IV) methyl-
prednisolone, methotrexate, azathioprine,
mycophenolate mofetil, IV immunoglob-
ulin, inﬂiximab (six infusions) and plasma
exchange were ineﬀective. Six cycles of the
B cell depleting antibody rituximab were
administered (dose: 375 mg/m
2). B cell
depletion was conﬁrmed by a CD19 count

of 0.001 · 109/l. Subsequently cerebellar
symptoms improved restoring ability to
eat using a fork and knife. Dysarthria also
improved, as did mobility and she was
able to walk using cross bars. Endo-
crinopathies were unaﬀected by immune-
modulation.
